mainEntity.name: Can my dentist polish my crown at a routine check-up?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, polishing a crown can form part of a routine hygiene or check-up appointment. Your dental professional will use appropriate polishing materials suited to your crown type. If your crown requires more specific attention — such as addressing a rough edge or surface damage — your dentist may schedule additional time to assess and treat this properly. It is always worth mentioning any concerns about how your crown looks or feels before or during your appointment so that your dental team can plan accordingly.

mainEntity.name: Will polishing change the colour of my crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Polishing can help remove surface staining and restore some of the original lustre to a crown, but it will not change the underlying colour of the material. Dental crowns — unlike natural teeth — do not respond to bleaching or whitening agents, so the base shade of your crown will remain as it was when it was fitted. If you are concerned about the colour match between your crown and surrounding teeth, this is worth discussing with your dentist, who can advise on the options available.

mainEntity.name: How long does a dental crown typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of a dental crown varies depending on the material used, where it is positioned in the mouth, and how well it is maintained. Many crowns can last ten years or more with appropriate care, regular dental check-ups, and good oral hygiene. Crowns in areas of heavy biting load — such as molar teeth — may be subject to more wear over time. Your dentist will monitor the condition of your crowns at routine appointments and advise you if replacement becomes necessary.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a crown to feel rough after it has been fitted?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some minor roughness immediately after crown placement is not unusual and may settle over the first few days as you adjust to the restoration. Your dentist will check the bite and margins at the time of fitting and make any necessary adjustments. If roughness persists, worsens, or is accompanied by discomfort, it is advisable to contact your dental practice to discuss this. A smooth, comfortable fit is important both for comfort and for maintaining good oral hygiene around the crown.

mainEntity.name: Can I use whitening toothpaste on my crowned teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whitening toothpastes are generally not recommended for use on crowned teeth. Many whitening toothpastes contain abrasive particles that can gradually damage the surface glaze of ceramic or porcelain crowns, making them more prone to staining rather than less. Additionally, the bleaching agents in whitening products have no effect on crown materials. A standard, non-abrasive fluoride toothpaste is typically the most appropriate choice for maintaining crowned teeth — your dentist or hygienist can advise on the most suitable product for your individual situation.

mainEntity.name: Does grinding my teeth damage my crowns?

acceptedAnswer.text: Bruxism — the clinical term for tooth grinding and clenching — can place significant forces on dental restorations, including crowns. Over time, this may cause surface wear, chipping, or damage to the margins of crowns, particularly those made from ceramic or porcelain. If your dentist has identified signs of bruxism, they may recommend a custom-fitted occlusal nightguard to protect your teeth and restorations during sleep. Early intervention is generally more straightforward than addressing advanced wear damage, so it is worth raising concerns about grinding with your dental team.
